text_blocks.snippet: To obtain a lift chair through Medicare, you'll need a prescription from your doctor and to purchase it from a Medicare-approved supplier. Medicare Part B (or a Medicare Advantage plan) typically covers the lifting mechanism of the chair, while the recipient is responsible for the remaining costs.
snippet_highlighted_words: you'll need a prescription from your doctor and to purchase it from a Medicare-approved supplier

list.title: Doctor's Prescription:
list.snippet: Your doctor must determine that a lift chair is medically necessary due to your condition, such as severe arthritis or a neuromuscular disease, and that you're unable to stand from a regular chair without assistance.

list.title: In-person Evaluation:
list.snippet: You'll need a face-to-face visit with your doctor to assess your mobility and document the need for the lift chair.

list.title: Certificate of Medical Necessity:
list.snippet: Your doctor may need to complete a "Certificate of Medical Necessity for Seat Lift Mechanisms" form, also known as Medicare form CMS-849.
Part B Coverage: Medicare Part B covers the electronic lifting mechanism of the lift chair.
Cost Sharing: You'll be responsible for 20% of the Medicare-approved cost of the lifting mechanism, as well as the cost of the chair's frame and upholstery.
Medigap: If you have a Medigap (Medicare Supplement) plan, it may cover the 20% that Medicare doesn't.

list.title: Medicare-Approved Supplier:
list.snippet: You must purchase the lift chair from a supplier enrolled in Medicare that accepts assignment.

list.title: Claim Submission:
list.snippet: The supplier will submit the claim to Medicare for the lift chair's lifting mechanism.

list.title: Eligibility:
list.snippet: Medicare may not cover a lift chair if you already have a wheelchair or scooter paid for by Medicare, or if you are in a hospital or skilled nursing facility.

list.title: Maintenance:
list.snippet: You may be responsible for the cost of maintenance or repairs after you assume ownership of the lift chair.

list.title: Cost:
list.snippet: Contact your doctor and supplier to get an estimate of your potential out-of-pocket costs.

list.title: Electronic Lifting Mechanism:
list.snippet: Medicare Part B covers the cost of the mechanical lifting component of the chair, not the chair itself or any accessories like cushions, fabric, or heating/massage features.

list.title: Medical Necessity:
list.snippet: The lift chair must be deemed medically necessary by a doctor, often due to conditions like severe arthritis or neuromuscular diseases.

list.title: Cost Sharing:

list.title: Coverage Similar to Part B:
list.snippet: Medicare Advantage plans are required to cover the same portion of the lift mechanism as Part B.

list.title: Additional Benefits:
list.snippet: Many Advantage plans may offer additional benefits or cover more of the cost, so it's important to check with your specific plan.

text_blocks.snippet: In summary, if you meet the criteria for a medically necessary lift chair, Medicare Part B or your Medicare Advantage plan can help offset the cost of the lifting mechanism.
